archetype.name: Dual-Threat (scramble-first)
archetype.definition: An accurate, rhythm-based passer whose second layer of value comes from escaping the pocket: he gains yards and first downs when plays break down, rather than from designed runs.

report.headline: Accuracy is back and the scrambles still work, but third downs cap the offense
report.take:
Daniels arrived as a rookie who did everything at once: 0.204 EPA per play (9th), a 3.5 CPOE and 891 rushing yards in 2024. Then came a 2025 in which the accuracy fell apart (CPOE -2.7, 44th) and the efficiency fell with it. The 2026 version has fixed the accuracy. His CPOE of 3.81 ranks 11th and is 6.5 points better than last year. His interception rate of 0.9 is 9th-best. He is still second among quarterbacks in rushing yards per game at 40. Yet passing EPA per dropback sits at 0.025, 25th of 54. He is completing throws he should complete, and the drives still stall.

The passing profile splits cleanly by depth. Between 10 and 19 air yards he has been outstanding: 0.619 EPA per attempt, a 68.4% success rate and an 18.5 CPOE on 38 throws, worth 23.5 EPA. Everything else is close to flat or negative. The 28 deep shots have connected 28.6% of the time with a -7 CPOE. The 22 throws behind the line have cost 7.6 EPA. The short game is steady (0.052) but slight. The legs fill the gaps. Scrambles come on 11.2% of dropbacks, average 0.562 EPA and have produced 11 first downs. His dropbacks total 16.9 EPA once those scrambles are counted, against 5.8 from passing alone. Designed runs, by contrast, have been poor (-0.433 EPA, 1.5 yards a carry). His running value is improvised, not schemed.

The averages hide two things. The first is third down, where he sits at -0.142 EPA with a 31.7% conversion rate, facing 7.5 yards to go on average and taking 8 of his 17 sacks. That is where the offense dies. The second is game state. Within one score he is at -0.046 EPA per play. Trailing by 9 or more he is at 0.175, with a 15.2 CPOE against softer coverage. The target mix matters too. Chig Okonkwo has drawn 35 targets at -0.144 EPA each. Antonio Williams has turned 26 into 0.628 apiece, and Stefon Diggs is a solid 0.299. One real gain deserves credit: his pressure-to-sack rate of 32.1% (26th of 42) is far better than the 41.2% and 43.9% that ranked near the bottom in his first two years.

Where it is heading: the recent line is mixed rather than rising. Over the last three games his yards per attempt is up (7.63) and passing yards are up to 246.7 a game. His CPOE has dropped to 0.3, his interception rate has climbed to 2.1% after a two-pick win over the Giants, and his rushing has shrunk to 22.3 yards a game. The line is also thinning. Starting guard Lucas Patrick is out with a concussion, and Laremy Tunsil is not expected back until late December.

strengths.title: Intermediate accuracy carries the passing game
strengths.body: Throws of 10-19 air yards produce 0.619 EPA per attempt with an 18.5 CPOE, and this one band supplies most of his passing value. It fits the accuracy rebound from last year. The exact rate will cool on a 38-attempt sample, but the skill behind it looks real.

strengths.title: Scrambles turn broken plays into gains
strengths.body: He scrambles on 11.2% of dropbacks at 0.562 EPA each, with 11 first downs. That keeps him second in rushing yards per game even though designed runs have gone nowhere. It is the most durable part of his profile, the same thing he did as a rookie, though it depends on his health and his willingness to run.

strengths.title: Fewer pressures turning into sacks
strengths.body: His pressure-to-sack rate of 32.1% is a clear break from the 41.2% of his rookie year, which ranked near the bottom of the league. He is getting rid of the ball or escaping more often, while his time to throw stays near 2.78 seconds. A three-year trait improving this much suggests a real adjustment, not noise.

concerns.title: Third downs stall the offense
concerns.body: On third down he is at -0.142 EPA with a 31.7% conversion rate, and 8 of his 17 sacks have come there. Partly this is situational: 7.5 yards to go on average is long, and pressure shows up on obvious passing downs. Even so, this is the biggest gap between his accuracy and his results, and the guard injury does not help.

concerns.title: Deep shots and screens are wasted plays
concerns.body: His 28 throws of 20+ air yards have hit 28.6% of the time with a -7 CPOE. The 22 throws behind the line have cost 7.6 EPA. The deep miss is partly the price of a low-percentage throw, but the screens are a scheme problem. Together they cap his efficiency.

concerns.title: Volume aimed at the wrong targets
concerns.body: Okonkwo is second on the team in targets at -0.144 EPA each. Antonio Williams, with fewer looks, has been the most efficient option. Within one score his overall efficiency is slightly negative, so the good numbers lean on trailing scripts. Shifting looks toward Williams is the cleanest internal fix.

trend.note: Passing yards have risen across the last five games and efficiency per dropback has held right at his season level. The last three games, though, show lower CPOE, more interceptions and much less rushing, so the profile is shifting more than improving.

nextGame.headline: Shootout script against Cincinnati should push his passing volume
nextGame.body:
Cincinnati's offense ranks second in passing EPA and leads the league in passing above expectation. Washington's pass defense ranks 22nd. The Book has the Commanders as 6.5-point home underdogs with a 52.5 total, which points toward Daniels throwing from behind, the state where he has been at his best. Cincinnati's defense is middling against the pass (11th) and soft underneath (24th on short throws), which suits his steady short game and his intermediate strength. It is stingy deep (6th), where he already struggles, and 9th in sack rate, which tests his weakest area. Opponents throw on this defense more than anywhere else, and tight ends have outscored their averages against it by more than any other team but two. That gives Okonkwo a chance to finally earn his volume.

On availability, guard Lucas Patrick (77% of snaps) is out with a concussion, a real interior downgrade against a defense that gets home. Tunsil remains on IR. Lead back Jacory Croskey-Merritt has not had his practice window opened, so the backfield likely stays with Rachaad White, whose targets have been inefficient. On Cincinnati's side, edge rusher Cashius Howell (39% of snaps) is on IR, which takes some sting out of the rush. Cornerback Jalen Davis has been designated to return and could add a body in coverage. Washington also gets 11 days of rest.

keyMatchups.title: Game script and passing volume
keyMatchups.body: A 52.5 total, a 6.5-point spread and a Cincinnati pass offense ranked second all point toward Daniels throwing often from behind. Trailing by 9 or more he has averaged 0.175 EPA per play.

keyMatchups.title: Pass rush vs a guard-less line
keyMatchups.body: Cincinnati's 9th-ranked sack rate meets a line missing Patrick. His improved pressure-to-sack rate gets a real test here, especially on third down.

keyMatchups.title: Soft underneath, tight end openings
keyMatchups.body: Cincinnati ranks 24th against short throws and has let lead tight ends beat their averages. That fits a game plan built on short and intermediate timing throws rather than the deep shots this defense takes away.

nextGame.watch: How often he escapes to scramble against Cincinnati's rush on third down; that decides whether the volume becomes efficient.

restOfSeason.body:
The accuracy rebound looks real. It shows up across depths, holds against his own 2025 and matches his rookie form, so the completion rate and low interception rate should mostly hold, though the two-pick game is a reminder that the interception rate will drift up. What should cool is the intermediate band's 18.5 CPOE and a red-zone touchdown haul built on few plays. The rushing should settle back toward 30-40 yards a game through scrambles, but the recent dip and the useless designed runs keep it from returning to rookie levels. Expect roughly 225-260 passing yards, 1.2-1.8 touchdowns, 25-40 rushing yards and 16-21 PPR points a game.

The ceiling depends on factors outside his control. A defense ranked 22nd should keep Washington throwing from behind, which helps volume and production. A thinning line, with Patrick out and Tunsil not due back until late December, keeps the sack and third-down problems alive. If the target mix tilts toward Antonio Williams and Diggs and away from Okonkwo, his efficiency could finally catch up to his accuracy.
swingFactors: Target share shifting to Antonio Williams

confidence.note: Seven games is a usable sample with career context, but the key splits rest on 20-40 plays each.
